Question: For a finite sequence \(A=(a_1,a_2,\ldots,a_n)\) of numbers, the Cesàro sum of \(A\) is defined to be \[ \frac{S_1+S_2+\cdots+S_n}{n}, \] where \[ \begin{aligned} S_k&=a_1+a_2+a_3+\cdots+a_k\\ &\qquad(1\le k\le n). \end{aligned} \] If the Cesàro sum of the \(99\)-term sequence \((a_1,a_2,\ldots,a_{99})\) is \(1000,\) what is the Cesàro sum of the \(100\)-term sequence \((1,a_1,a_2,\ldots,a_{99})?\)
